text:
maya (pm): Quick sync — customer asks keep landing on this thread. Major ask: customers want deterministic latency guarantees across geos + tenant isolation tiers. Need to land roadmap asks, cutover acceptance criteria, and clear cost tradeoffs by EOW.

linh (eng-plat): Can we scope this into two milestones? 1) routing policies + soft-affinity fallback, 2) hard tenant lanes + eviction semantics. Each with acceptance tests.

maya (pm): +1. Proposed acceptance for milestone 1:
- 95th p95 <= 120ms for regional traffic (internal perf test)
- fallback to compatible model variant without request failure
- rollout procedure documented in Console

adrian (infra): Need infra checklist: AZ pair capacity buffer, cross-region bandwidth limiters, and routing policy API. Also need a migration plan for existing tenants pinned to old lanes.

kevin (sre): Don't forget SLO burn alerts. If we switch to soft-affinity, we should detect cross-region spill and auto-throttle non-critical tenants.

sofia (sales): Heads up: two enterprise pilots (FinCorp + Healthly) require regulatory isolation and monthly cost cap. They expect a private deployment option in pilot. This will change rollout gating.

linh (eng-plat): For the routing policy API sketch: 
```
policy {
  match: { tenant_id: string }
  route: { region_preference: [eu-west-1, us-east-1], fallback: nearest }
  lane: { isolation_tier: shared|reserved|dedicated }
}
```
Need a CLI + console surface.

maya (pm): Great. Add launch criteria for pilots: 
- Private deployment validated (Healthly)
- Cost cap enforcement implemented (billing hooks + per-tenant quota)
- Runbook for cross-region failover tested in canary group

adrian (infra): Implementation concerns: reserved lanes require dedicated pools -> capacity commit or autoscaling w/ cold-start ramp. That affects pricing model. We should present options: monthly reserve vs dynamic reserved (burstable).

kevin (sre): Action: create chaos test plan for cutover that simulates region loss and tenant eviction. Must include rollback path and metrics to validate graceful degradation.

sofia (sales): For prioritization: if FinCorp signs for dedicated lanes we'll accelerate hard-isolation. Need a decision ticket that ties budget to implementation path.

linh (eng-plat): Dependency list: model-variant compatibility matrix (research), kernel selection guardrails (runtime), Console UI for policy editing (frontend), billing hooks (finance).

maya (pm): My proposal for prioritization this sprint:
- Sprint A: policy API + fallback routing + basic console view + perf tests (milestone 1)
- Sprint B: reserved lanes prototype + billing hooks + canary with 2 customers (milestone 2)
- Sprint C: private deployment hardening + compliance checklist + ramp docs

adrian (infra): Sounds feasible if we get one infra hire and the research team to finalize quantization compatibility by mid-sprint.

kevin (sre): I'll take the chaos plan and SLO alerts work. Will create runbooks and PagerDuty playbooks.

sofia (sales): I'll flag FinCorp + Healthly timelines and negotiate trial terms to align with Sprint B.

maya (pm): Cool — I'll write the decision ticket and acceptance checklist. Will @everyone in the roadmap doc once done. Any blocking asks?

linh (eng-plat): Need research confirmation on fallback model quality delta. If fallback degrades user experience we need quality-monitoring tied to rollouts.

maya (pm): Noted — add to acceptance: quality thresholds for fallback (we'll define eval prompts).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for routing-policy-api on staging at 1765554360 :rocket:

adrian (infra): Nice — will monitor egress and cross-region path metrics.

kevin (sre): I'll watch SLO dashboard. Report back in ~30m with initial numbers. :eyes:

maya (pm): Thanks team. I'll convert this thread into the roadmap PR with explicit launch gates.
